what_it_does: Satellites in low Earth orbit (roughly 500 km up) increasingly carry cameras and sensors that generate far more data than can be beamed down to Earth in real time; one solution is to put small servers with AI accelerator chips on the satellites themselves, processing images in space. But nobody had a rigorous cost framework for deciding what hardware to put up there. This paper builds a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) model — accounting for the cost of electric power (which is scarce in space), the mass launched (launch is expensive per kilogram), the hardware price, and the communication bandwidth bought — and uses it to explore how different chip choices, satellite constellations, and design strategies compare in overall cost and capability.
